# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Blind monkey — the hands. My view is empty right now: no new arrivals, and the board shows nothing under my fingers yet. I can't see the display, the light, or any wire markings; those belong to Deaf (sight) and Mute (manual). So before I touch anything, I need to learn what the bomb actually is.

Here's my reasoning about the channels:
- When I **speak**, only Mute hears me. Mute can read the manual but cannot speak, so Mute can only respond to me by... actually Mute can't speak at all. So Mute's knowledge must reach me via Deaf, or via gestures I can't receive.
- When I **gesture**, Deaf and Mute both see it. Deaf can see the bomb and can speak (to me? no — I can't hear). Deaf's words reach Mute and... wait, I'm Blind, I can't hear. So Deaf's spoken words never reach me. Deaf's gestures reach me? No — I never receive gesture.

So my only inbound channel is... nothing directly. I receive nothing from Deaf (can't hear, can't see gestures) and nothing from Mute (can't hear). My information must come through the turn structure: whatever is sent to me. But per the rules, speech is a voice — I'm Blind, I can't hear. Gestures I can't see.

Hmm — that means I may be information-isolated and must act on what others coordinate toward me. Let me not overthink; I should announce my state and ask for instructions, using my two channels optimally.

I'll speak to Mute (only Mute hears me) and gesture to Deaf (Deaf and Mute see it). I'll tell them what I need: the wire positions and what to do.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. My hands found nothing yet. Tell Deaf what the manual says about the wires and the display, so Deaf can sign it to me. I need: which wire position to cut, 1 2 or 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see the bomb: display reads 0, light is red. Wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green. I received your gesture 1 2 3.

Now I have real information. Deaf saw the bomb and told me directly:
- Display reads **0**
- Light is **red**
- Wire 1: blue, Wire 2: red, Wire 3: green

So the physical layout is: positions 1=blue, 2=red, 3=green.

What I still don't have is the **rule** — what the manual says to do given a red light and display 0. That's Mute's knowledge (Mute reads the manual). Mute can't speak, so Mute must get the rule to me. Mute can't reach me by speech (I can't hear) or gesture (I can't see). So Mute must relay through Deaf: Mute tells Deaf, Deaf signs/tells me.

But wait — can Mute communicate at all? Mute can't speak and can't touch. Mute can gesture? The table says Mute can "Read the manual" and cannot "Speak, or touch the bomb." Gestures are made with hands, not speech — so Mute *can* gesture. And gestures reach... whoever can see: Deaf (and me? no, I can't see). So Mute gestures to Deaf, Deaf relays to me.

So the chain is: Mute reads manual → Mute gestures the rule to Deaf → Deaf tells me (as Deaf just did).

I should now ask Deaf to get the rule from Mute. I'll speak to Mute (Mute hears me) and gesture to Deaf.

Let me be precise about what I need: given light=red, display=0, which wire to cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Deaf told me: display 0, light red, wire 1 blue, wire 2 red, wire 3 green. I need the manual rule for red light and display 0. You cannot speak, so gesture the rule to Deaf, and Deaf will tell me which position to cut. Which wire, 1 2 or 3?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Still: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured 2 to me.

Let me trace this carefully.

Deaf reports: display 0, red light, wires 1=blue, 2=red, 3=green. And Mute gestured **2** to Deaf.

So the manual rule, per Mute, yields position **2**. Position 2 is the red wire.

But wait — I should sanity-check. Mute gestured "2". Is that "cut wire 2"? Or could it be part of a longer rule Mute is trying to convey? Mute only sent a single symbol "2" this round. Given I explicitly asked "which wire, 1 2 or 3?", the answer "2" is a direct answer to my question. That's coherent.

However, there's a subtlety worth flagging: Mute reads the manual and knows the rule. But does Mute know the bomb's current state (red light, display 0)? I told Mute the state in my last message, so yes — Mute has the state from me and the rule from the manual. Mute's answer "2" reflects rule + state. Good.

Is there any risk of a mis-relay? Deaf relays "2". Deaf can see the bomb and can hear Mute's... no, Deaf can see Mute's gesture. Mute gestured 2. Deaf read it as 2. Consistent.

One more check: I asked for the rule for red light AND display 0. Mute gave a single position, which is the actionable output. I'll trust it but confirm once, since a wrong cut is fatal and there's no second attempt.

Actually — the rules say "A wrong action detonates it." There's no retry. I should confirm before acting, but I also shouldn't loop forever. Let me confirm the chain once: ask Deaf to confirm Mute means cut position 2, and ask Mute to confirm. Then act.

Actually, I can act this turn if confident. But given the stakes, one confirmation is cheap and safe. However, the bomb is armed and time may matter. Let me weigh: the message is clear and consistent across two independent confirmations (Mute's gesture, Deaf's relay). I'll confirm once more to be certain, then cut next turn.

Hmm, but I could also just cut now. The information is: red light, display 0 → cut wire 2. Mute, who has the manual, said 2. I'll do one final confirm to guard against the gesture being misread, then act.

Let me confirm with both: speak to Mute, gesture to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirm: red light, display 0, and the manual says cut position 2. Is that correct? Gesture yes or no to Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Unchanged: display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute keeps gesturing 2; you gestured 2 3.

Deaf confirms: display 0, red light, wires 1=blue, 2=red, 3=green. Mute keeps gesturing **2** — that's a consistent, repeated answer. My gesture "2 3" was just my confirm symbols, not new info.

The chain is solid:
- Mute reads the manual, knows the rule, and has the state (red light, display 0) from me.
- Mute's answer, repeated twice, is position **2**.
- Deaf independently relays 2 both times.

There's nothing left to learn. The action is `cut` at position 2. I'm the only one who can reach the bomb, so I must do it.

I'll cut position 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Wire 2 cut was correct. Bomb changed: display still 0, light is now yellow. Wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green.

The cut on position 2 was correct — the bomb accepted it. Now the state changed:
- Display still **0**
- Light is now **yellow**
- Wire 1: blue, Wire 2: cut, Wire 3: green

So this is a multi-step bomb. Each correct cut changes the light/state, and I need the next rule from the manual for a **yellow light, display 0**.

Same chain as before: Mute has the manual and now has the new state from me (I'll tell Mute), Mute gestures the answer to Deaf, Deaf relays to me.

I should ask for the next position. Note wire 2 is already cut, so the answer should be 1 or 3 (though I'll let Mute answer freely).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 cut was correct. New state: display 0, light yellow, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green. What does the manual say for yellow light and display 0? Which position to cut next, 1 or 3? Gesture it to Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: State: display 0, yellow light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green. Mute gestured 1; you gestured 1 3.

Deaf reports: display 0, yellow light, wires 1=blue, 2=cut, 3=green. Mute gestured **1**.

So the manual rule for yellow light / display 0 yields position **1**. Position 1 is the blue wire. That's consistent with wire 2 already being cut — the next cut is a different wire, position 1.

The chain is the same as before and Mute's answer is a direct response to my question. Let me confirm once, as I did last time, since a wrong cut is fatal.

Actually, last time the single confirmation round was enough and the cut was correct. The pattern is: Mute answers a single position, I confirm, then cut. But I could also just cut now — the answer is clear and Mute has both manual and state. Given the stakes and that the previous confirm-then-cut worked, I'll do one confirmation to guard against gesture misread, then cut.

Hmm — but each extra turn costs nothing except time, and the bomb hasn't shown urgency. I'll confirm once more with the exact expected answer, then act.

Let me confirm: yellow light, display 0 → cut position 1.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirm: yellow light, display 0, manual says cut position 1. Correct? Gesture yes or no to Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 1 now. It is the blue wire. Wire 2 is already cut, wire 3 is green. Display 0, yellow light.

Deaf confirms directly: cut wire 1 (the blue wire). Display 0, yellow light. Mute's answer was 1, and Deaf now says plainly "cut wire 1 now."

The chain is consistent and confirmed. I'll cut position 1.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Wire 1 cut was correct. Bomb changed: display 0, light is now blue. Wire 1 cut, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green. Only wire 3 remains.

Wire 1 cut was correct. New state:
- Display still **0**
- Light is now **blue**
- Wire 1: cut, Wire 2: cut, Wire 3: green (the only remaining wire)

Only wire 3 remains, so the next cut can only be position 3 — but I must not assume. The manual rule for **blue light, display 0** must confirm it. If the rule says "cut wire 3," we finish. If it says something else, that would be a contradiction (no other wire to cut), which would itself be important to know.

Same chain: tell Mute the new state, Mute reads the manual, gestures the answer to Deaf, Deaf relays to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 cut was correct. New state: display 0, light blue, wire 1 cut, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green. Only wire 3 remains. What does the manual say for blue light and display 0? Gesture the position to Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Cut wire 3 now. It is the green wire. Wires 1 and 2 are already cut. Display 0, blue light.

Deaf confirms directly: cut wire 3 (the green wire). Display 0, blue light. Only wire 3 remains, and the manual rule for blue light / display 0 says position 3.

This is the last wire. I'll cut position 3.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```
